resources.description: Free clothes, shoes and linens in Gilbert. No appointment or referral; bring photo ID or ask about a temporary ID accommodation.
resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
One Small Step’s Clothes Cabin gives free clothing, shoes, household linens and hygiene items. Back to Work helps with required workwear and a pair of work shoes for a new job. Unsheltered clients can also use showers, weekly laundry, lockers and mailboxes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For anyone who cannot afford the items needed. Clothing visits are once every three months, for yourself, your partner and your children under 18. Bring current photo ID of any kind; ask about a temporary accommodation if you are obtaining ID. Work items require new-hire papers, an employer letter or the Back to Work request form. Staff may ask for guardianship information when you collect clothing for children.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit during client hours; no appointment or referral is needed. For a new job, bring its clothing requirements and employment evidence. For help, call 480-285-4111 or email info@onesmallstepaz.org. If you cannot visit because of a crisis or transportation problem, ask your service provider about PINCH pickup. Clothes Cabin accepts requests from local service providers; your helper should confirm they can use it. Work shoes still require a new job.

**Access**
The building is at the back of the business park. Children cannot enter the shopping area; if they come, they must stay in the small playroom or lobby. Arrive at least one hour before closing for showers and two hours before closing for laundry.

**Important Information to Know**
Quantities depend on stock. The FAQ usually allows 4–7 clothing items plus socks and underwear, and one set of sheets, one blanket or one set of towels per visit; ask about that day’s limits. Clothes Cabin closes for holidays, the day before Thanksgiving, the Christmas–New Year week and the last week of January. Donation and paid resale-shop hours differ from free client hours.
resources.name: Clothes Cabin · Clothing, Workwear, Linens and Hygiene

openQuestions.question: Can TSO missionaries use PINCH to collect items for someone who cannot visit?
openQuestions.explanation: Clothes Cabin invites local service providers to request small emergency orders for people in crisis, without transportation, or otherwise unable to visit. Providers collect under their agency information; the page does not name TSO or explain whether its missionaries qualify. Call 480-285-4111 to confirm who can request and collect an order, using https://www.onesmallstepaz.org/pages/pinch. Do not promise pickup until that is settled. The ordinary walk-in service remains available without a referral.

resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Clothing visits every three months include five outfits, shoes, pajamas, underwear, socks and accessories. Children can also receive books, hygiene products, diapers and infant supplies. Birthday, back-to-school and holiday programs provide additional items.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For foster and kinship children, including some children without a DCS case. Bring Notice to Provider paperwork for foster placements. Unlicensed kinship caregivers can use Notice to Provider or a Kinship Number from a partnering program; court guardianship is also accepted. Ask about eligibility for a young adult.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-969-5411 to book. Bring the care paperwork each visit. Biological or adopted children in a family with a current foster placement may receive one outfit, books and gifts; bring their birth certificates.

**Access**
Appointments are at 126 E. University Drive in Mesa during Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Tell staff about urgent placement needs and ask how to obtain a Kinship Number if you need one.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general-public closet. Confirm sizes and seasonal enrollment when scheduling. For someone over 18, ask specifically about boutique eligibility; AZURA also runs a separate Foster360 housing and coaching program.

resources.hours: Winter adult outreach (October–May): Monday and Thursday noon–3 p.m. Confirm current summer weekday hours. Summer family evening: Sunday 5–8 p.m., through September 27, 2026.
resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Friends at First offers adult clothing, showers, hygiene items, food, phone charging and a place to rest. Adults may choose five clothing or shoe items per visit. Staff can help connect people to community services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adult outreach serves people experiencing homelessness or hardship. The sign-in form asks for state-issued ID, but the website does not say whether someone without ID can still receive help. Ask staff rather than assuming you cannot be served.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-969-5577 or email friendsatfirstmesa@gmail.com. Ask which adult days are operating this month. The church lists Monday and Thursday noon–3 p.m., with lineup from 11 a.m., no earlier. Ask for help checking in if you cannot complete the online form.

**Access**
The outreach building is at the southeast corner of the church parking lot on First Avenue. Monday/Thursday noon–3 is the published October–May winter schedule. A separate summer family evening offers cooling, showers and basic help on Sundays 5–8 p.m., through September 27, 2026.

**Important Information to Know**
The adult closet does not currently advertise children’s clothing. Ask before bringing a child for clothes. The Sunday family program is separate and seasonal; it does not promise hotel placement. First Community Missions operates Friends at First from the church site.
resources.name: Friends at First · Adult Clothing, Showers and Basic Needs

resources.hours: Boutique/career center: Mon-Thu 9 AM-4:30 PM; Fri closed; second/fourth Sat by appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Free professional clothing and job-search support for women. Get an interview outfit; after a job offer, return for a week of work clothing. Career help includes resumes, cover letters, interview practice, coaching and job-retention support. Fast Track offers one-day or four-day job-search training.

EducateHER helps with college certificates and the support needed to finish, including possible tuition, childcare, living-expense stipends and emergency aid. Digital and financial-literacy training are also offered.

The Mobile Career Center takes clothing and coaching to community sites. A separate Workforce Initiative offers job-readiness classes, clothing, employer connections and help such as bus passes, gas cards or certifications for teens and young adults.

Tailor Made for Success separately offers men interview clothing, resume and interview help, and career coaching. HOPE for Success provides reentry support through a separate program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
General services are for women and do not require a referral. Clothing is for interviews and starting work. Ask staff about any program-specific requirements.

EducateHER requires an application, intake interview, admission to a participating school and an eligible certificate choice. Confirm the current funding criteria. Childcare aid is for eligible children age five and younger; a stipend requires active participation.

The Workforce Initiative serves ages 16-24, including high school students and recent graduates, through school/community partnerships.

Tailor Made serves unemployed and underemployed men. Ask its staff about appointment requirements and any costs; the main women’s program rules do not automatically apply.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-489-7397 or email services@dfsarizona.org. Explain whether you need clothing, career help or education support. Walk-in suiting is welcome during regular service hours; advance contact helps staff prepare. Schedule Saturday visits in advance.

For EducateHER, start at https://educateherphx.org/ or ask staff for application help. Confirm admission and financial support before committing to a course. For mobile or youth services, ask for the next Mesa location and enrollment route.

For men’s Tailor Made services or a satellite appointment, call the same number and name the program. Use the current Fast Track event link from Client Services, or ask staff which session to register for.

**Access**
Boutique and Career Center: Park Central, Diamond Building, 3110 N. Central Ave., Suite D-200, Phoenix, AZ 85012. Monday-Thursday, 9 AM-4:30 PM; closed Friday. Second and fourth Saturdays by appointment only. Relay: 711.

Mobile services go to partner sites; a current Mesa schedule is not confirmed. Ask about transportation, language help and disability accommodations when planning your visit. Satellite options are listed in Glendale, Peoria and at Paradise Valley Community College. Arrange the specific site and appointment before traveling; these listings do not establish a Mesa mobile stop.

**Important Information to Know**
General programs are offered at no cost. EducateHER may cover up to full tuition and eligible childcare costs, but funding and approved courses vary. Confirm what is covered, any remaining school costs and the requirements for keeping support.

Donor drop-off hours differ from client-service hours. For reentry-specific enrollment, ask about the separate HOPE for Success program.

resources.description: Helps you find temporary, part-time or full-time work with local employers. There is no job placement fee. Call for help applying by phone or in person.
resources.hours: Monday–Thursday 8 AM–5 PM; Friday 8 AM–3 PM
resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
One application connects you with several employers. Jobs may include warehouse and manufacturing work, skilled trades, office and customer service work, and professional roles. Temporary, evaluation-hire and direct-hire options depend on current openings. Express offers weekly pay and free online job-search resources. ExpressLearn courses are for workers employed by Express. Some workers qualify for health-plan options, dental, vision, life and disability coverage, retirement benefits and confidential counseling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements depend on the job, including experience, skills, schedule and any required license. Some jobs require a skills assessment. Placement depends on a suitable opening. Some benefits require a minimum number of hours or weeks worked; ask which benefits you qualify for, what they cover and what you would pay.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-820-3700 to arrange help with an application by phone or in person, or email jobs.mesaaz@expresspros.com. You can also apply online. Have your work and education history, references and contact details ready. Bring work-eligibility documents to an interview; ask which documents you need. If you create an online account, submit your application to the Mesa office; saving an account alone does not send it.

**Access**
849 N. Dobson Rd., Suite 107, Mesa, AZ 85201. Office hours: Monday–Thursday, 8 AM–5 PM; Friday, 8 AM–3 PM. Call before visiting to arrange application help. Job locations vary by employer.

**Important Information to Know**
Job placement is free. Before accepting work, ask about the pay, schedule, work location, transportation and any required equipment or testing costs. Openings change; applying does not guarantee a job. After an assignment ends, contact the office to be considered for another one.

**Eligibility Requirements**
County services generally serve Maricopa County residents outside Phoenix; Phoenix has its own program. Adult individualized career services require age 18+ and permission to work in the U.S. Training has additional eligibility checks. Priority goes to people receiving public assistance, people with low income or basic-skills needs; veterans and eligible spouses within these groups receive top priority.

Youth: in-school ages 14-21 need low income and a qualifying barrier. Out-of-school ages 16-24 need a qualifying barrier. English learners may qualify under the in-school route. Ask staff about other routes if these do not fit.

**Programs and Services**
Free help with job searches, resumes, interviews and career planning. DES also has two specialized routes:

• Vocational Rehabilitation (VR): help when a disability makes work difficult. An individual employment plan may include training, job coaching, placement, transportation or workplace changes.
• Reentry services: job preparation, referrals, workplace skills and coaching for people returning from incarceration or with past justice involvement. Follow-up help may continue after someone gets a job. Ask about transportation or clothing help when available.

Veterans and people with disabilities can receive additional employment support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
General job-search help is available to job seekers. VR has a separate assessment: a physical or mental disability must make getting or keeping work difficult, and VR services must be needed and able to help with an employment goal.

Reentry help includes people in prison or on parole preparing to return home and previously incarcerated job seekers. Ask staff which program fits; requirements for county Smart Justice are not automatically the rules for DES reentry services.

Veterans and eligible spouses receive priority for qualifying employment services. Specific training, funding and specialist support have their own requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
For VR, call 800-563-1221. Staff can help complete a referral and arrange a local appointment. The VR webpage also has English and Spanish referral forms, including large-print versions.

For general job help, call 833-762-8196, visit an ARIZONA@WORK office or request a Google Meet appointment at https://workappointment.azdes.gov/. In Mesa, the East Valley Career Center is at 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101; 602-372-9700.

For reentry help, use Request Employment Services on the DES reentry page or ask the local ARIZONA@WORK office. The online request requires an email address; call or visit if that makes the form difficult to use.

**Access**
Statewide, including Mesa. VR’s directory lists Chandler-Mesa staff at 125 E. Elliot Rd., Chandler, AZ 85225; 602-771-5949. Another nearby VR office is 11518 E. Apache Trail, Suites 114-121, Apache Junction, AZ 85120; 480-983-0427.

Call before traveling to confirm the right office, appointment and staff availability. RSA may arrange phone, virtual or community-location meetings. A VR office inside Mesa city limits is not confirmed. Ask about language help or disability accommodations when scheduling.

VR eligibility and funded services are decided individually. Ask your counselor about any waiting period, which training or equipment is approved, and any costs you must pay before agreeing to services. Reentry transportation and clothing help depend on availability.

If you disagree with a VR decision, DES says to request an appeal in writing within 20 calendar days after receiving the decision letter. The Client Assistance Program can help: 602-274-6287 or 800-927-2260.

Job-search specialists cannot resolve unemployment claim questions. For those, DES lists 877-600-2722.

before.address: East Valley Career Center, 1001 W Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85210
before.description: Free job-search and career help in Mesa, with training guidance, youth services and Smart Justice reentry support.
before.hours: East Valley center: Mon-Thu 8 AM-7 PM; Fri 8 AM-5 PM. Specialist appointments may differ.
before.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Free help choosing a career, finding job openings, preparing resumes and interviews, and using computers. Ask about skills training, paid work experience, internships and apprenticeships. Training and placement depend on eligibility and available opportunities.

Youth services can include GED/education support, mentoring, career planning and paid work experience. Ask about help with transportation, testing fees or training costs. Workshops cover resumes, interviews, computers, money management, office skills, workplace readiness, entrepreneurship and CPR/first aid. The CPR class is not Basic Life Support certification.

Smart Justice helps eligible people with felony convictions prepare for work, discuss their background with employers and find opportunities. The center also lists DES employment, reemployment-assessment and veterans services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
County services generally serve Maricopa County residents outside Phoenix; Phoenix has its own program. Adult individualized career services require age 18+ and permission to work in the U.S. Training has additional eligibility checks. Priority goes to people receiving public assistance, people with low income or basic-skills needs; veterans and eligible spouses within these groups receive top priority.

Youth: in-school ages 14-21 need low income and a qualifying barrier. Out-of-school ages 16-24 need a qualifying barrier. Examples include homelessness, foster care, pregnancy/parenting, disability or justice involvement; leaving school without a diploma can qualify out-of-school youth. English learners may qualify under the in-school route. Ask staff about other routes if these do not fit.

Smart Justice: age 18+, authorized to work, a felony conviction, and currently on probation/parole or released within the past year. People laid off or affected by a closure, lost self-employment, displaced-homemaker or military-spouse circumstances should ask about Dislocated Worker eligibility.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the East Valley Career Center at 602-372-9700 and explain the help you need. Staff can help create an Arizona Job Connection account at the center. For individual services, use the county Client Portal at https://hsdclientportal.maricopa.gov/; staff will contact you to arrange an appointment. Call if you need help with these steps.

Ask which documents to bring. The program checklist may include photo ID, Social Security card, income records for the past six months, DD214 for veterans and Selective Service records when applicable. Youth also need proof of their eligibility circumstances. Ask staff what to do if documents are missing.

For workshops: 602-506-0589 or HSDTrainingTeam@maricopa.gov. The training page also offers an online Registration Request. Office-skills assessments need an appointment.

For Smart Justice: 602-372-1839 or WDDSmartJustice@maricopa.gov. Ask about its appointment and community-site schedule.

**Access**
East Valley Career Center: 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa. Hours: Monday-Thursday, 8 AM-7 PM; Friday, 8 AM-5 PM. Closed weekends. Relay: 711. Confirm specialist and workshop times.

Some resume, financial and basic-computer workshops are offered in Spanish; ask for the next session. Disability accommodations are available on request.

The Mesa Workforce Center/MesaCAN partner is at a different address: 635 E. Broadway Rd., second floor, Mesa; 480-769-7417. The City lists Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 8:30 AM–2:30 PM, with Wednesday by appointment. Confirm the specific service before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
A referral or application does not guarantee a training grant, apprenticeship or job. Ask which costs and supports are covered before committing to training. Ask Smart Justice about transportation or interview-clothing help; availability is not guaranteed. For VR, ask whether the center provides appointments or refers you to the state rehabilitation office.

Unemployment benefits are handled by DES, not awarded by the county career center. Staff can direct you to the appropriate DES application route.

Career coaches help with resumes, practice interviews, job searches and employer connections. Free training ranges from computer basics and Microsoft Office skills to selected industry credentials. Goodwill says general career services are open to anyone at no cost. You must be at least 13 to register for a MyCareerAdvisor account. Individual courses and in-person services may have their own requirements; ask about your chosen service.

Call 602-535-4444 for career help, or complete the Connect with a Career Coach form on Goodwill’s Career Services page. You can also create a MyCareerAdvisor.com account. If you need in-person help, call before traveling and explain whether you are a veteran and what help you need.

resources.description: Free job-search help and work clothing, plus a separate housing program for qualifying full-time workers. Start at the Mesa office.
resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Free job planning, employer referrals, resumes, interview preparation and interview clothing. Uniforms, safety shoes, tools and transportation help may be available; ask about the items and limits.

The separate Workforce Housing program offers 90 days in shared housing, weekly support, life-skills classes and follow-up after moving out. Ask about room privacy and the length of follow-up; the provider’s pages give different descriptions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Job-search services are free for unemployed or underemployed people. Newly employed assistance generally requires permanent/direct-hire W-2 work, 25–40 hours weekly, at least minimum wage and a start within the past 30 days. Required screenings must be completed. Temporary, seasonal, staffing-agency and app-based jobs do not qualify for that extra assistance.

Workforce Housing has separate rules. Its housing page requires full-time, direct-hire W-2 work paying at least $18 an hour, plus 30–45 days on the job or at least two pay stubs. Participants commit to saving 80% of take-home pay, weekly meetings and first-month workshops. Some felonies are considered individually. Job-search eligibility does not establish housing eligibility.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk into 1833 W. Main St., Suite 128, Mesa, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–noon or 1–4 p.m.; closed noon–1 p.m. No appointment is needed. Call 602-755-5627 with questions. Bring photo ID, a phone and a resume if available; ask for help if these are missing.

**Access**
The office is near the Sycamore/Main Street light-rail stop. For newly employed assistance, have the employer email jobs@theworkeraz.org from a company address with your full name, start date, pay and weekly hours. This is separate from starting a job search. For Workforce Housing, use the Apply to Workforce Housing link at https://www.theworkeraz.org/get-housing or ask staff for application help. The page advertised a two-to-three-month wait when checked September 9, 2026; confirm today’s estimate. Ask about location and costs. The Mesa office is not a housing unit.

**Important Information to Know**
The newly employed resources are offered once and depend on supplies. Ask staff which clothing or equipment they can provide before purchasing it. The organization also uses the name St. Joseph the Worker. Housing is a separate program. The site describes low living costs but gives no current amount; ask about rent, deposits and other charges before agreeing to a place. Do not assume the free job-search service means free housing.

**Programs and Services**
Pays approved refundable security deposits to the landlord. Utility deposits can be requested with the security-deposit application. This is deposit help, not payment of overdue rent or ordinary monthly utility bills.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The new rental unit must be in Mesa. Apply before signing the lease or moving in. The landlord and utility provider must accept the City’s payment guarantee and program terms, and the unit must pass inspection. Ask staff to check the current household-income and residency rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Housing at 480-644-3536 to confirm current intake and funding, then use the program’s online application or ask for a paper form. The saved FY25/26 paper form asks for photo ID for the household head, Social Security cards for household members, an unsigned proposed lease, income records and two recent full bank statements. Ask for the current form and checklist, and help obtaining missing documents. The current online application could not be read during this check. For utility deposits, get an account and deposit letter from the utility provider.

If you cannot upload documents, that paper form lists fax 480-644-2923 or the secure drop box at 200 S. Center St., Building 1. Label them with your name and “Security Deposit Application.”

Housing questions can also go to housing.info@mesaaz.gov.

**Access**
Office lobby: Monday–Thursday, 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; Housing Specialist visits need an appointment. Ask for help completing the application if needed.

**Important Information to Know**
Start well before the move. The saved FY25/26 paper form asks for at least 14 days on its first page, says 10 days on its last page, and estimates 10–14 business days to process. Confirm the actual timeline with Housing. Approval also requires inspection; an application is not a promise of payment. Help covers approved refundable deposits, with the rental deposit capped at two months’ rent on that paper form. Utility-deposit help requires rental-deposit approval.

The new rental unit must be in Mesa. Apply before signing the lease or moving in. The landlord and utility provider must accept the City’s payment guarantee and program terms, and the unit must pass inspection. Ask staff to check the current household-income and residency rules.

Office lobby: Monday–Thursday, 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; Housing Specialist visits need an appointment. Ask for help completing the application if needed.

Start well before the move. The linked form asks for at least 14 days on its first page, says 10 days on its last page, and estimates 10–14 business days to process. Confirm the actual timeline with Housing. Approval also requires inspection; an application is not a promise of payment. Help covers approved refundable deposits, with the rental deposit capped at two months’ rent on the linked form. Utility-deposit help requires rental-deposit approval.

resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
UMOM runs this countywide entry service for families. Staff explore safe options and referrals; the Hub is separate from UMOM’s shelters.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families with children under 18. Have every adult needing shelter join the call, with household names, ages and tonight’s safety information.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 211 or 877-211-8661, daily 9 a.m.–7 p.m.

**Access**
If directed, or unable to call, Mesa families can use MesaCAN, 635 E. Broadway Rd., Tuesday 9 a.m.–3 p.m.

**Important Information to Know**
Screening is free. Shelter priority depends on need and available beds, not who called first. Answer calls from unfamiliar numbers and tell staff if your situation changes. Ask how often to check in; call 211 if your waitlist status becomes inactive.

resources.address: Administrative office: 6935 E. Williams Field Rd., Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.description: Year-long housing for qualifying families with children or someone in the third trimester of pregnancy. Rent is $400 a month including utilities; income and work requirements apply.
resources.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
A temporary family home, case manager, furnishings, food and clothing, with help toward work and stable housing. Resident children can use on-site activities and learning support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
You must live in Arizona and be homeless, have an eviction notice or be fleeing domestic violence. You need custody of a minor child living with you, or be in your third trimester. At least one adult must be 18. Document at least $1,170 monthly income throughout the application and stay; cash jobs do not count. Background and drug screening apply; sex offenses exclude applicants.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the Need Housing page for its Housing Inquiry Form. If the form is unavailable or you need help, call 480-988-9242. Eligible families are considered when space opens.

**Access**
Homes are in Mesa. The administrative office is at 6935 E. Williams Field Rd.; arrange intake before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
The stay is one year. Rent is $400 monthly including utilities, with a $200 deposit and $400 last month’s rent due at move-in. If your starting income is not from work, you must be able to find employment within 45 days. This is not immediate shelter; call 211 if you need a place tonight.
